assertions.assertion: The patient presents with recurrent episodes of palpitations and lightheadedness consistent with supraventricular tachycardia, which have become more frequent despite current medical management.
The patient has a significant history of transient ischemic attack and cerebral infarction.
Prolonged cardiac rhythm monitoring is indicated to evaluate for potential arrhythmic triggers and guide further therapeutic intervention.
CPT 93271 Cardiac Event Monitoring is supported.
Diagnosis codes I47.1 and Z86.73 are associated with the service.
The payer's denial under PR-204 states that this service is not covered under the member's current benefit plan.
The claim for Cardiac Event Monitoring (CPT 93271) has been denied.
The determination is based on Reason Code PR-204, indicating that this specific service is not covered under the member's current benefit plan.
Coverage determinations are strictly governed by the terms of the active policy, and this procedure falls outside the scope of reimbursable services.
The patient has the right to appeal this decision.
To initiate an appeal, submit a formal request along with supporting clinical documentation to the Appeals Department within the timeframe specified in the member's Summary of Benefits.
Failure to submit timely appeals may result in the forfeiture of appeal rights.
